about: The site's tone, as rules a machine can check (gate 4). A careful, diplomatic, non-political tone that separates known, inferred and uncertain facts, all sourced. Any match in 'hold' keeps a record out of the site until it is reworded; 'review' asks the monthly reviewer to look again (gate 5). Grow these lists from each month's findings.

people.about: Records describe institutions and evidence, not individuals. No journalist, official or private person is named in record text; authors appear only inside a source's citation.

evidence.rule: A record whose text uses projection words cannot be marked known.

voice.about: Humility. Common Shade describes what helps, what it depends on and who could act; it does not instruct anyone. In the site's own voice, prefer could, can, would ideally, works best when, is worth checking, is fairer when. A law, a standard or a physical limit may be stated as it is (In Singapore, employers must give...), and quoted headlines keep their own words. tools/check-voice.js reads every built page: a phrase on the hold list fails the build unless its sentence contains an allowed phrase.
allow: air conditioners must carry an energy label
air conditioners must meet a higher minimum efficiency
banks must check whether a borrower
planes need longer runways or must carry less
whether she should go back at all
active cooling where it is essential

suspicion.about: Words that suggest wrongdoing by someone, even when the sentence says it was not found ('no mis-selling alleged'). A denial still plants the idea, so the site describes what it could and could not see instead. Checked on every page by tools/check-voice.js.
